content_units: Cape Town Household Fit

For this household,   Fibre Plus 100/50 Mbps at ZAR 999   is the best value. It stays under the   ZAR 1,200   budget, gives materially better   upload speed   for cloud backups and video calls, and is the strongest balance of   reliability, headroom, and cost  .
Plan Value Comparison
Plan   Price   Speed   Best For   Main Risk   Verdict
Fibre Basic   ZAR 799   50/25 Mbps   Smaller households, lighter backup use   Less upload headroom during simultaneous calls + streaming   Good budget pick
Fibre Plus   ZAR 999   100/50 Mbps   Two remote workers, 4K streaming, frequent video calls   Slightly higher monthly spend than Basic     Best value
Fibre Max   ZAR 1,299   200/100 Mbps   Heavy power users, large backups, many devices   Over budget   Strong but fails budget
LTE Home   ZAR 699   40/10 Mbps, 500 GB cap   Light use, backup connection   Lower reliability than fibre; cap risk; weak upload   Not ideal for this use case
Why Fibre Plus Wins
-   Reliability priority:   Fibre is typically more stable than LTE for work-from-home use, especially for long video calls.
-   Upload speed matters here:     50 Mbps upload   is much better suited than 25 Mbps or 10 Mbps for:
- cloud backups
- simultaneous Zoom/Teams calls
- large file syncing
-   Enough headroom for real overlap:   Two remote workers plus one 4K stream can comfortably fit on   100/50 Mbps   without running as close to the limit as 50/25 Mbps.
-   Still under budget:   At   ZAR 999  , it leaves about   ZAR 201   below the cap while avoiding the compromises of LTE and the overspend of Fibre Max.
Best Option and Trade-offs
Recommended:   Fibre Plus 100/50 Mbps   Best blend of upload speed, reliability, and price under budget     ZAR 999

Use-Case Notes
Context used:
- Two remote workers likely need   2 concurrent HD video calls
- One 4K stream typically needs a solid chunk of download bandwidth
- Frequent backups benefit noticeably from   50 Mbps upload
- Uncapped fibre is safer than a   500 GB LTE cap   for a work-heavy household
